text.p: China Resources (Holdings) has mandated five banks as lead arrangers for a US$250 million syndicated term loan facility, NatWest Markets said on Thursday.
The five banks are BA Asia, DKB Asia, NatWest Markets, Sakura Bank and Sumitomo Bank.
The facility has a maturity of five years and will be repaid in five equal semi-annual installments after three years' grace.
The interest margin is 0.40 percent per annum.
The lead arrangers will invite the relationship banks of the CRC group to join as arrangers and underwriters on Thursday.
Proceeds of the loan will be used for refinancing and for general corporate funding.
China Resources (Holdings) is a Hong Kong-based conglomerate under the direct control of China's Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation (MOFTEC).

It mainly engages in trading, property development, transportation and warehousing, retailing, infrastructure, telecommunications and other business areas. China Resources Enterprises and Ng Fung Hong Holdings are the two principal Hong Kong-listed subsidiaries of CRC.
Last week, bankers said that with fees, they expected the loan to pay an all-in return of less than 50 basis points.
